newsitem.title: UK: Ldn Freight - Capers are subdued.
newsitem.headline: Ldn Freight - Capers are subdued.

text.p: The freight market has continued the week relatively quietly and activity in the Caper and Handy-Sizes has been especially subdued.

Caper brokers seem generally agreed that February will remain lacking in serious positive features for owners, but many also consider the market fundamentals to be sound and potential for March to be good.

Panamax turnover is down but fixtures originating in the Atlantic appear steady. The BFI was up one point at 1375 reflecting the uncertainty of the current market, and the Baltic Handy Index fell 10 points to 1006.

Caper and two Panamaxes have been reported fixed in the U.S. Gulf/Continent. Cargill booked Dimitrios for about 90,000 grains Mississippi to Amsterdam for mid-Feb at $1M lumpsum, reckoned equivalent to about $11.10 basis 55', compared to Bunge's fixture last week of Captain Veniamis at $10.55.

Details of payments of over-age insurance premium were not disclosed. Cargill also booked the 1974-built Cornilios ina prompy position (believed to be in place of a late-running Handy-Size) for 53,000 heavy grain Mississippi/Amsterdam at $11.90 (compared to $11.50 fixed last week to Ghent for Feb 18/25).

Continental were understood to have taken the Navios-Reflet Polmar 73,000 DWT delivery U.S. Gulf Feb 10 laydays for a trip to Hamburg option Israel, but full details were lacking (Reports of $11.00 basis heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Hamburg were discounted.

Halla were reported to have conceded a stronger $13,500 daily for New Horizon 66,742 DWT delivery prompt Gibraltar trip Far East, although it was not clear if the loading intention was via U.S. Gulf or east coast of South America.

Among new orders quoted on Tuesday were Continental's 50/60,000 heavy grain plate and Brazil/Iran for Feb 13/19 and a geared Panamax delivery plate prompt/on for 4-6 months Timecharter, Bluedeck 1.7/2.5M CFT grain delivery SW pass Feb 20/25 trip Egypt, and Soufflet 8,500 WHT Rouen/Italy prompt.
The Indian government was reported to have purchased another 250,000 tonnes of Australian Wheat.
Reports circulated in a thin Caper market that Mosk fixed Tien Shan 128,826 DWT for coal from Banjermasin to Rotterdam at $7.85.

British Steel failed Mineral Europe 170,000 DWT delivery S. Korea end Feb trip via W. Australia redelivery U.K. at about $13,500 daily and fixed instead Doceriver for 150,000/10 Ironore Cape Lambert/Redcar at $8.00 or $8.25 (But E vessel is waiting 11 days to present.)
In the Atlantic Safore were linked with Obo Selim for 90,000 coal Norfolk to Richards Bay but a rate was not disclosed.
This section of the market has remained flat in most areas. The 1982-built Serafin Topic 37,188 DWT was rumoured fixed by EACC delivery Nopac trip Far East at $7,500 daily plus $150,000 bonus.
